exposure: maternal body habitus (body mass index of ≥40 kg/m(2))
Maternal age of 15 years or younger
Infants who did not receive whole-body cooling
cohort: Live-born singleton infants delivered at or beyond 36 weeks' gestation
finding: Umbilical cord prolapse, placental abruption, and uterine rupture were the strongest factors associated with infant cooling for neonatal encephalopathy.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was associated with an increased risk of infant cooling in the univariable analysis, but not after staged-stepwise logistic analysis.
